description:
A capacity planner needs to analyze server resource usage to prepare for scaling decisions. You are provided with a CSV file located at /home/user/data/server_usage.csv containing daily records of CPU and memory usage for multiple servers. Your task is to transform this data to help visualize peak usage patterns and identify candidates for scaling. Here’s what you should do, step by step: 1. Read the file /home/user/data/server_usage.csv. Each row contains:
  • Date in YYYY-MM-DD format
  • Server name (e.g., server1, server2, etc.)
  • CPU usage in percentage (e.g., 78.5)
  • Memory usage in MB (e.g., 2048)
Example row: 2024-06-05,server1,78.5,2048 2. For each server, find the day with the highest CPU usage (peak CPU day), and the day with the highest memory usage (peak memory day). 3. Create a new report file at /home/user/data/peak_usage_report.csv with the following columns (header must be included):
  • Server
  • Peak CPU Date
  • Peak CPU Value
  • Peak Memory Date
  • Peak Memory Value
4. In your output file, each row should represent one server, and the values should be separated by commas. Example of a row: server1,2024-06-05,78.5,2024-06-04,2564 5. For verification purposes, create a log file at /home/user/data/report_generation.log. This log file should contain exactly two lines:
  • First line: "Peak usage report generated successfully."
  • Second line: "Output file: /home/user/data/peak_usage_report.csv"
Please read the input file carefully and ensure that your output format matches the descriptions above exactly – including column names, order, comma separation, and log messages. The automated test will verify both the content and format of your output files.
